dublinCore.description: Step-by-step flip-and-slide demonstration of the convolution integral. The impulse response is time-reversed, shifted by t, multiplied by the input, and the area under the product is plotted as the output y(t) for eight pairs of signals.

topic: Impulse response of an LTI system
learningObjectives: Explain each step of the convolution integral: flip, slide, multiply and integrate
Identify the range of t over which two finite-duration signals overlap, and so where the output is non-zero
Predict the shape of the output for simple pairs of signals before stepping through them
Calculate y(t) at one time from the overlap region and its area
Describe how the shape of an impulse response determines what a system does to its input
prerequisites: Impulse response of an LTI system

misconceptions.misconception: Convolution multiplies the two signals point by point
misconceptions.correction: The shaded product is a whole function of tau for one value of t, and only its area is one point of the output
misconceptions.evidence: Move the Time t slider and watch the product change shape while its area traces the purple output curve

misconceptions.misconception: The output has the same duration as the input
misconceptions.correction: The output of two finite pulses lasts as long as the sum of their durations
misconceptions.evidence: Rectangle * Rectangle: two 2 s pulses give a 4 s output

misconceptions.misconception: The impulse response slides without being reversed
misconceptions.correction: The curve that slides is h(t - tau), a function of -tau, so it is the mirror image of h
misconceptions.evidence: Rectangle * Exponential: h decays to the right but the red curve decays to the left

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Flip-and-slide convolution. Top plots show the input x(t) and impulse response h(t). The middle plot shows x of tau, the flipped and shifted h of t minus tau, and their shaded product. The bottom plot traces the output y(t), the area of the product, as time t advances.

controls.label: Signals
controls.description: Chooses which pair of signals x(t) and h(t) is convolved

controls.label: Play / Pause
controls.description: Sweeps t automatically from its current value to 7 s; restarts from -2 s if t is already at the end

controls.label: < Step
controls.description: Pauses and moves t back by 0.25 s

controls.label: Step >
controls.description: Pauses and moves t forward by 0.25 s

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Pauses and returns t to -2 s

controls.label: Time t (s)
controls.description: Sets the shift t of the flipped impulse response h(t - tau)

controls.label: Play speed
controls.description: Seconds of t swept per second of real time while playing

visualElements.description: Small plots of the input x(t) in blue and the impulse response h(t) in red
Plot against tau of x(tau), the flipped and shifted h(t - tau), and their shaded product
Output y(t) traced up to the current time, with a marker at the current area
Read-out of t and the value of the convolution integral, plus a one-line note on the selected pair

model.description: Evaluates the convolution integral with the midpoint rule at a step of 0.005 s over tau from -1 to 16 s; all signals are zero for t < 0
equations: y(t) = integral of x(tau) h(t - tau) d tau

instructionalStrategies: Predict the output by sketching it, then step through to check
Step-through worked example with a numeric read-out at every t
extensions: Swap the roles of x and h and confirm that the output is unchanged (commutativity)
Relate the output duration to the sum of the two input durations
